issue.title: StatementError.__str()__ does not obey contract of its superclass SQLAlchemyError.__str()__

labels.name: engine
labels.description: engines, connections, transactions, isolation levels, execution options

issue.body:
Looking at class `SQLAlchemyError` it seems that the idea is to return `unicode` string from `__str()__` method.
For example `__unicode()__` method [looks](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/rel_1_3_0b1/lib/sqlalchemy/exc.py#L57-L58) like this:

```python
    def __unicode__(self):
        return self.__str__()
```
However `StatementError` class which inherits `__unicode()__` method from `SQLAlchemyError` class implements its own `__str()__` which returns `str` string not `unicode` string. This results in returning `str` string from `StatementError.__unicode()__` which is not right. Looking at implementation of `__str()__` in `StatementError` class it seems there is nothing which would prevent using `unicode` format string instead of `str` one when constructing return value thus resolving the issue.

All of the above is concerned with Python 2.

issue.title: _Error.message should be unicode not str also in Python 2

repository.name: python-cx_Oracle
repository.description: Obsolete Python interface to Oracle Database, now superseded by python-oracledb

issue.body:
`_Error.message` is [described](https://cx-oracle.readthedocs.io/en/latest/module.html#cx_Oracle._Error.message) as:

> String attribute representing the Oracle message of the error. This message is localized by the environment of the Oracle connection.

The problem is the type of this attribute in Python 2 is `str` not `unicode` which basically means we get encoded form of the error message and no information what encoding it is.

The `message` attribute is created in `cxoError.c` like [this](https://github.com/oracle/python-cx_Oracle/blob/7.0/src/cxoError.c#L160-%3EL161):

```c++
    error->message = cxoPyString_fromEncodedString(errorInfo->message,
            errorInfo->messageLength, errorInfo->encoding, NULL);
```
and `cxoPyString_fromEncodedString` is defined in `cxoModule.h` like [this](https://github.com/oracle/python-cx_Oracle/blob/master/src/cxoModule.h#L49) (for Python 2):

```c++
    #define cxoPyString_fromEncodedString(buffer, numBytes, encoding, errors) \
        PyBytes_FromStringAndSize(buffer, numBytes)
```

body:
in #4430 (can we make these just one issue since they are closely related?)  you said "Looking at implementation of __str()__ in StatementError class it seems there is nothing which would prevent using unicode format string instead of str one when constructing return value thus resolving the issue." which seems like a proposal for a fix.

it would make things easier for me if you could either show me a complete test case showing a problem to resolve or could propose how you see the code being fixed.   the former is more generally useful since I can also make that the test.

See here is what I mean:

```
# coding: utf-8

from sqlalchemy import exc

message = u"méil"

def illustrate_plain_python():
    obj = Exception(message)
    try:
        print(obj)
    except Exception as e:
        print("illustate plain raised: %s" % e)

def illustrate_sqlalchemy_exc():
    obj = exc.SQLAlchemyError(message)
    try:
        print(obj)
    except Exception as e:
        print("illustate sqlalchemy exception raised: %s" % e)


illustrate_plain_python()
illustrate_sqlalchemy_exc()
```

run in Python 2:

```
illustate plain raised: 'ascii' codec can't encode character u'\xe9' in position 1: ordinal not in range(128)
illustate sqlalchemy exception raised: 'ascii' codec can't encode character u'\xe9' in position 1: ordinal not in range(128)

```

behavior is identical.  Where's the bug that's specific to SQLAlchemy ?    the comment inside of private message _message() is not particularly useful but that's a private method anyway.
just for issues of management i want to keep this all on #4430 so we can figure out what the canonical approach is for this.

The illustration for this problem is the code

```python
# coding: utf-8

from sqlalchemy import exc

message = "méil"

def illustrate_plain_python():
    obj = Exception(message)
    try:
        print(obj)
    except Exception as e:
        print("illustate plain raised: %s" % e)

def illustrate_sqlalchemy_exc():
    obj = exc.SQLAlchemyError(message)
    try:
        print(obj)
    except Exception as e:
        print("illustate sqlalchemy exception raised: %s" % e)


illustrate_plain_python()
illustrate_sqlalchemy_exc()
```

run in Python 2:
```
méil
illustate sqlalchemy exception raised: 'ascii' codec can't decode byte 0xc3 in position 1: ordinal not in range(128)
```

@marc1n ah, you mean, when the non-ascii is passed as a bytestring, now that is interesting!  OK....now, I think I need to see how that happens, is this basically the connect error I see in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/4430#issuecomment-452649543 ?     Is there another case where this happens on a running connection and the error message comes back not decoded?

the case that @mekk gave me for https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/4430#issuecomment-452649543 is not reproducing here, maybe because this is oracle express or something:
```

$ NLS_LANG="POLISH_POLAND.AL32UTF8" python
Python 3.7.0 (default, Jun 28 2018, 10:59:55) 
[GCC 8.1.1 20180502 (Red Hat 8.1.1-1)] on linux
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import cx_Oracle
>>> cx_Oracle.connect(user="nobody", password="nopass", dsn="127.0.0.1")
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
cx_Oracle.DatabaseError: ORA-12541: TNS:no listener

```

is there another setting I can change to get it to spit out non-american messages?   I'd like to see if i can even get the test suite to run like that.

OK here is major scientific discovery number one:

```
#! coding: utf-8

raise Exception(u"select méil FROM dual")

```

```
~/.venv2/bin/python2 test.py
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test.py", line 3, in <module>
    raise Exception(u"select méil FROM dual")
Exception: <exception str() failed>

```

wow!   you can't put a u'' in a Python 2 exception with non-ascii chars (I'm assuming this is based on my platform settings)!  

so the choices are:

1. pass through bytestrings direclty

2. convert to a u'' but use ascii with errors="replace"

so...#1 is a bigger change, but that passes the characters right through.   #2 is a much safer change but you'd get ugly looking error messages.

mind blown, not a bug report, not eight years old, just a 1.2 regression in 064f82986c, no tests to see that it broke.    

I prefer very much if folks can just show me the code that's "not working" up front, that can save a lot of time, thanks!
